title: Translate a signature
prompt: Implement remaining(hp, damage), clamped at zero. Example: remaining(20, 30) is 0.
tests:
assert remaining(100,30)==70, '100 HP minus 30 damage should be 70'
assert remaining(20,30)==0, 'HP must not go below zero'
solution:
def remaining(hp, damage):
    return max(0, hp-damage)

assert scaled(0,-1,1000)==(0,-1000), 'Respect the supplied unit factor'

title: Preserve a snapshot
prompt: Given {'units': [{'hp': number}, ...]}, return an independent copy with damage removed from the first unit, clamped at zero. Example: 100 HP and 30 damage gives 70 without changing the input.
tests:
s={'units':[{'hp':100},{'hp':50}]}
b=branch_hit(s,30)
assert b['units'][0]['hp']==70, 'Branch should receive damage'
assert s['units'][0]['hp']==100, 'Original state must stay unchanged'
b['units'][1]['hp']=0

assert branch_hit({'units':[]},4)=={'units':[]}, 'Empty state should remain valid'

title: Sequential reductions
prompt: Apply an integer keep-percent twice, rounding down after each stage. Example: reduced(133,40) is 21.
tests:
assert reduced(133,40)==21, '133 should reduce to 53 then 21'
assert reduced(147,40)==23, '147 should reduce to 58 then 23'
assert reduced(3,60)==0, 'Round at each stage: 3 to 1 to 0'
assert reduced(10,100)==10, 'Keeping 100 percent preserves damage'
hint: Do not combine the two percentages before rounding.
